original_value: The diffuse attenuation coefficient of downwelling irradiance (Kd) is an essential parameter for inland waters research by remotely sensing the water transparency. Lately, Kd semi-analytical algorithms substituted the empirical algorithms widely employed. The purpose of this research was to reparametrize a semi-analytical algorithm to estimate Kd and then apply it to a Sentinel-2 MSI time-series (2017–2019) for the Três Marias reservoir, Brazil. The results for the Kd semi-analytical reparametrization achieved good accuracies, reaching mean absolute percentage errors (MAPE) for bands B2, B3 and B4 (492, 560 and 665 nm), lower than 21% when derived from in-situ remote sensing reflectance (Rrs), while for MSI Data, a derived MAPE of 12% and 38% for B2 and B3, respectively. After the application of the algorithm to Sentinel-2 images time-series, seasonal patterns were observed in the results, showing high Kd values at 492 nm during the rainy periods, mainly in the tributary mouths, possibly due to an increase in the surface runoff and inflows and outflow rates in the reservoir watershed.

result.paraphrase: The diffuse attenuation coefficient of downwelling irradiance (Kd) is a key parameter in inland waters research because it enables remote sensing of water transparency. Recently, semi-analytical Kd algorithms have replaced the empirical approaches that were widely used. This study aimed to reparameterize a semi-analytical algorithm to estimate Kd and then apply it to a Sentinel-2 MSI time series (2017–2019) for the Três Marias reservoir in Brazil. The semi-analytical reparameterization produced good accuracy, with mean absolute percentage errors (MAPE) below 21% for bands B2, B3 and B4 (492, 560 and 665 nm) when derived from in situ remote sensing reflectance (Rrs); for MSI data, the derived MAPE was 12% for B2 and 38% for B3. After applying the algorithm to the Sentinel-2 image series, seasonal patterns emerged, with elevated Kd values at 492 nm during rainy periods, especially at tributary mouths, possibly because of increased surface runoff and inflow and outflow rates in the reservoir watershed.
